name: Lanzarote
title: Holidays in Lanzarote
intro: Volcanoes, black lava fields and calm golden beaches, with warm sunshine right through Christmas. Here's what Lanzarote is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: October to April is the best time for winter sun, at around 20 to 23°C, though it can be breezy. Christmas and New Year are the busiest and dearest weeks. Summer is hot and dry.

things.name: Timanfaya National Park
things.blurb: Ride a coach through a moonscape of volcanoes and watch guides cook chicken on the heat from the ground.

things.name: Papagayo beaches
things.blurb: Sheltered golden coves in the far south with calm, clear water.

things.name: Jameos del Agua
things.blurb: A lava cave with a glowing lagoon of tiny blind white crabs, designed by local artist César Manrique.

things.name: Cueva de los Verdes
things.blurb: A guided walk through a long lava tube, with a surprise at the end.

things.name: Rancho Texas Lanzarote Park
things.blurb: A Wild West animal park with sea lion and birds of prey shows.

things.name: Teguise Sunday market
things.blurb: The island's biggest market, in the old capital every Sunday morning.

faqs.question: Is Lanzarote good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. The flight is about four hours, it's warm all winter, and Playa Blanca and Puerto del Carmen have calm, shallow beaches.

faqs.question: Is it warm at Christmas?
faqs.answer: Yes, usually around 21°C in the day. It can be windy, so a sheltered beach helps.

faqs.question: Which resort is best for families?
faqs.answer: Playa Blanca is quieter with calm beaches. Puerto del Carmen is livelier, with more restaurants and a long sandy beach.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: A week is ideal for beach days plus a couple of trips to the volcanoes and caves.
